abstract: Although the Williams syndrome transcription factor (WSTF/BAZ1B) is an established tyrosine kinase for histone H2AX, its broader substrate repertoire and functional importance in cancer pathogenesis remain elusive. Here, we show that WSTF directly phosphorylates AKT1 at tyrosine 417 (Y417), thereby promoting AKT1 activation. This phosphorylation is removed by the phosphatase EYA3, forming a dynamic regulatory node that fine-tunes AKT activation. Our study suggests that WSTF cooperates with PI3K-generated phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate (PIP3), which facilitates AKT1 recruitment to the cell membrane, allowing it to assemble with 3-phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase 1 (PDK1) and mTORC2 for activation. Consequently, genetic ablation of WSTF suppresses AKT pathway activity and inhibits tumor growth in both cell-based and xenograft models. Our findings suggest WSTF is a non-canonical activator of oncogenic AKT signaling and provide a rationale for developing selective WSTF inhibitors as potential therapeutics in AKT-driven cancers.
